The absence of constitutional symptoms and trauma lowers suspicion for septic arthritis or systemic illness, but does not exclude it. Thus, the only diagnosis fully supported by *all confirmed facts* — and *only* those facts — is the one that reflects the *objective, measurable, and unambiguous pathophysiologic process present*: **inflammatory arthritis**, defined by clinical signs (swelling, pain) + objective systemic inflammation (elevated CRP/ESR). All other labels (gout, PsA, etc.) require additional data not yet available. Among all causes of acute monoarthritis, **crystal-induced arthritis accounts for ~50–60% of cases in emergency/rheumatology settings**, with gout and CPPD together dominating.
